title: A Whip Crack Is a Sonic Boom. The Tip Breaks 767 mph

scenes.text: A whip crack is a sonic boom.
It's not leather hitting leather. It's the tip breaking the sound barrier. 767 miles an hour.
The whip tapers. So as the wave runs toward the thin end, it speeds up.
By the tip it's moving over 30 times faster than where it started. Faster than sound. Crack.
High-speed cameras proved it in the 1920s. Twenty years before any plane managed it.
Long before any jet, people were already breaking the sound barrier. With a whip.

description:
The crack of a whip is a small sonic boom. As the loop travels down the tapering whip it speeds up, and by the tip it can be moving more than 30 times faster than at the handle, past the speed of sound (about 767 miles an hour).
High-speed photography in the 1920s showed the tip going supersonic, two decades before Chuck Yeager flew faster than sound in 1947. Mathematicians at the University of Arizona worked out the full mechanism in 2002.
What other everyday thing do you think breaks the sound barrier? Comment below.

first_comment: A wet towel snapped hard enough can do the same thing, and so can a ping pong ball fired from a vacuum cannon at over 900 miles an hour. What would you try to make go supersonic?
